title: Fourier tail bounded by squared error
statement: Let $f$ and $g$ be real-valued functions on the binary cube of dimension $n$, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. If the Fourier degree of $g$ is at most $k$, then the sum of the squares of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ on subsets of size greater than $k$ is at most the uniform average of $(f(x)-g(x))^2$ over the cube.
hypotheses_covered: Real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on the binary cube of dimension $n$
The Fourier degree of $g$ is at most $k$
